scope: W6 formatting and checkstyle G1-G5, W7 final-fix01, W8 flake-fix01, W9 ED-05 pin fix, REL-001 patches A and B, REL-001/D4 launch deadline
mode: read-only; no Gradle, vitest or build run; no source edited

labels.V: read the code or evidence and saw it

findings.title: Hard teardown reports success when it found nothing to kill, so fail-closed does not hold for a PID-1 worker or an unreadable process table
findings.scenario: A launch hangs (Chrome frozen). Deadline fires; hardTeardown runs killLaunchTree. (a) Worker runs as PID 1 in a container (the existing Dockerfile pattern is CMD ["node", ...] with no init): canEnumerateProcessTree() passes at guidedMain.ts:24 because ps lists pid 1 as self, but selectLaunchRoots returns [] for parentPid <= 1 (tree.ts:311). (b) ps times out or fails: readProcessTableWithArgs returns [] (tree.ts:270-278). In both cases killLaunchTree returns [], survivorsOf([]) returns [] at once (tree.ts:356), hardTeardown continues to disposeScratch() (browser.ts:683) and resolves. GuidedRuntime.closeResources sets browserClosed = true, so GuidedOwnership.occupied() turns false and the single slot is released over a live browser, and the profile directory is removed under it. The ruling (sections 1 and 3.5) promises the slot is never released over a live browser.
findings.verified: Read the three code sites. tree.test.ts asserts selectLaunchRoots(TABLE, 1, [SCRATCH]) is [] and killLaunchTree(..., readTable: () => []) is [] and signals nothing, so the empty result is intended for selection but nothing downstream treats it as unverified. No test or code distinguishes 'nothing to kill' from 'could not look'. grep of helm-chart finds no guided deployment, and the README starts the worker with npm run start:guided (npm is the parent), so PID 1 is not a live configuration today. On this host ps shows orphaned Chrome-for-Testing pids 13577 and 13581 (ppid 1, up 3.5 days), so leaks do occur here.
findings.inferred: That a future guided Deployment overriding command to node dist/run/guidedMain.js would be PID 1; that ps timeouts occur in practice under load.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed on 'could not look': in killLaunchTree/hardTeardown throw when the table has no row for process.pid (reuse canEnumerateProcessTree(table)). In guidedMain insist process.pid > 1 (or allow parentPid 1 when running as the container init). Add a unit test for both. Not gate-affecting; fix or accept in writing before the worker ships in a container.

findings.title: A Chrome that spawns more than about 1 s after the teardown starts escapes both listings
findings.scenario: The deadline fires while launchPersistentContext has not yet spawned Chrome (host under I/O pressure; attempt03's Chrome was 3.9x slower than median). hardTeardown lists once (nothing), waits at most 1 s for the abandoned launch, lists again (nothing), survivorsOf([]) is clean, scratch is removed, the slot is released. Chrome then spawns against a deleted profile directory; Playwright's own timeout backstop (deadline + 3 s) ends it, but the ruling notes Playwright's timeout cleanup may try a graceful close for up to 30 s first.
findings.verified: Read hardTeardown and the ruling's note on coreBundle.js:39831-39871.
findings.inferred: The spawn timing and the 30 s graceful close behaviour were not reproduced.
findings.recommendation: Accept as a narrow double-fault window, or keep the slot held until the abandoned launchPersistentContext promise settles (as releaseWhenLaunchSettles does for the runtime-level hang).

findings.title: Only the launch phase is hard-killed; later start steps and non-deadline launch failures still close gracefully and unbounded
findings.scenario: The browser launches, then blankMatches() (a CDP call) hangs because the page is wedged. bounded() ends the start at 12 s with phase BLANK_MATCH. ownership.context awaits stopEntry, whose closeResources runs browser.close() (acquired.close()) with no bound. If the wedged browser also hangs the close, stop never settles, no reply is sent (backend gives up at 15 s with plain UNKNOWN_OUTCOME) and the slot is held indefinitely. The same applies to a launch that fails for a non-deadline reason and takes the graceful cleanup() path.
findings.verified: Read runtime.ts closeResources and browser.ts catch block. Ruling section 1 'Not in scope' defers bounding the close of a started session to D5.
findings.inferred: That a wedged page also hangs context.close(); not reproduced.
findings.recommendation: Record as a Known limitation referencing D5. The ruling trade-off sentence 'slot occupancy is bounded at about 15 s' is only true for the launch phase.

findings.title: The 'inside the backend's 15 s window' assertion cannot fail, and the ignoring-launcher path replies at the ceiling, not inside it
findings.scenario: The test advances the fake clock by exactly GUIDED_START_BUDGET_MS + GUIDED_START_RESERVE_MS (15 000) and then asserts Date.now() - began <= 15_000. The clock cannot be anywhere else, so a regression that delayed the reply further (up to the fake clock's end) would still pass. Separately, for a launcher that ignores the abort the reply is 12 s (start) + 3 s (closeResources endedWithin) = 15.0 s, so the backend sees plain transport UNKNOWN_OUTCOME rather than CONTEXT_LOST, which the ruling acknowledges.
findings.inferred: Real network timing of the reply relative to the backend's 15 s timer.
findings.recommendation: Assert on when the promise settles (advance in smaller steps and record the first tick at which pending settled) and state expected reply time per launcher type; or drop the claim from the comment.

findings.title: The survivor path (close() rejects, slot stays held) is untested, and the recording-directory assertion is trivially true
findings.scenario: Mutation: make hardTeardown ignore survivors (browser.ts:682) or make GuidedLaunchFailure.close swallow its error. No unit test has a failed-launch close that rejects (the only close-rejection test, runtime.test.ts:272, is for a started browser), and the fixtures test only covers the case where every pid dies. Also, Chrome is frozen at PROCESS, before any video file exists, so readdir(dir) equals [] holds without exercising partial-webm cleanup after a kill in APP_PAGE.
findings.verified: Grepped test/guided for GuidedLaunchFailure constructions: all close arguments resolve. Read the fixtures test: the watcher freezes the first Chrome child at spawn. Dex discloses that only the PROCESS sub-step is proven against real Chrome.
findings.inferred: That a mid-launch kill leaves a partial webm that the recorder's UNAVAILABLE settle then removes (ruling section 3.4); not demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Add a runtime unit test where GuidedLaunchFailure.close rejects: stop() rejects CONTEXT_LOST, active stays true, a new assign is refused CAPACITY. Optionally a fixtures case that freezes after the recording starts.

findings.title: Removing .filter({ hasText }) from the version probe leaves every unit test green
findings.scenario: Mutation: change page.locator(selector).filter({ hasText: /\S/u }).waitFor(...) to page.locator(selector).waitFor(...). On the real chrome://version page both elements exist (empty) at load, so the wait returns immediately and the original race returns. In the fake, filter is () => locator(selector) and ignores its argument, and waitFor itself models 'settles only when populated', so the tests still pass. Dex's M5 mutation (read before waiting) is caught; this one is not. Only a real-Chromium case with injected lag would catch it, and none is committed (the lag experiment lived in the repro harness).
findings.verified: Read the fake and the source.
findings.inferred: That the real race is as described in root-cause.md; the root cause of attempt03 is unproven, per Dex.
findings.recommendation: Make the fake's filter record its argument and return a locator whose waitFor only settles if the hasText filter was applied, and assert hasText.test(' ') is false and hasText.test('x') is true.

findings.title: View on the three deviations from the D4 ruling (Aria rules)
findings.scenario: (1) stop() rejects CONTEXT_LOST for a launcher that never settles: agree; the ruling's test table ('stop() resolves') contradicts its own 'treat it like any close failure' text, and resolving over a held slot would answer a stop 200 while occupied() stays true. entry.stopping then caches the rejection, so a retry never re-attempts teardown; release is through releaseWhenLaunchSettles. (2) context() ignores a failing stopEntry: agree; wire parity holds (409 CONTEXT_LOST both ways, HEAD already threw bare CONTEXT_LOST after the stop), slot occupancy is read from runtime.active, and a test asserts GuidedStartFailure is still thrown while the slot is held. (3) microtask turns instead of the 3 s reserve: agree; the real launcher needs about 3 ticks against a budget of 16, the fallback in closeResources collects a slower one within 3 s, and the only loss is the sub-step in the log line. Caveat: the real tick count is not pinned by any test (the unit fake is one hop).
findings.verified: Read runtime.ts, ownership.ts, browser.ts catch block and the unit tests.
findings.recommendation: Ratify all three. Amend the ruling's test-table row for the hung launcher from 'stop() resolves' to 'stop() rejects CONTEXT_LOST after the reserve; slot held'.

findings.title: Logging residues: a 64-bit hash prefix of the session id, and a message echoed when it looks like a closed code
findings.scenario: GUIDED_START_FAILED carries hash(sessionId).slice(0,16): unsalted SHA-256 of a UUID, so it is a stable correlation token (the sidecar file name already uses the full hash) and not the id; not reversible for a v4 UUID. describeLink echoes error.message verbatim when it matches ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,47}$; an error whose whole message were an all-capitals secret-like token would be logged. No such throw site exists in the start path.
findings.verified: Read the code; transport.test.ts plants a private path and the session id and asserts neither appears.
findings.inferred: No future code throws a caps-only secret as a message.
findings.recommendation: No change needed. If 'no session id in any form' is a hard rule, drop the hash prefix from the line.

findings.title: The startup guard probes ps -A -o pid=,ppid=, but the kill depends on ps -A -ww -o pid=,ppid=,args=
findings.scenario: On an image whose ps lacks -ww or the args column (BusyBox), the guard passes and every kill finds nothing (see F1). The pinned Playwright noble image has procps, so not an issue today.
findings.inferred: Behaviour of ps on other images.
findings.recommendation: Guard with readProcessTableWithArgs() and require a non-empty args for the worker's own row.

findings.title: 12 s start budget has about 4 percent headroom over the slowest measured start, and a refusal looks like REL-001 on the wire
findings.scenario: Ruling evidence: 2302 starts, slowest 11.50 s, p99 9.44 s (throttle plus cpu). A gate host with Spotlight and a Gradle JVM alongside is the environment where attempt03's Chrome ran 3.9x slower than median. A legitimate slow start now ends in 409 CONTEXT_LOST at 12 s, the same wire symptom as REL-001. The innermost link code TIMEOUT in the GUIDED_START_FAILED line tells them apart.
findings.inferred: How often a gate host exceeds 12 s.
findings.recommendation: When triaging a gate red, read the GUIDED_START_FAILED line first. Do not read a D4 timeout as REL-001 recurring.

findings.title: Optional startup argument and a default budget in the launcher are the only compat-shaped accommodation
findings.scenario: launch(..., startup?) is optional 'so existing fakes stay valid' and launchGuidedBrowser uses Date.now() + 12 s when it is absent. Production (guidedMain) always passes it through GuidedRuntime. Not a second path in production; it is the sort of default the single-path rule is meant to keep from spreading.
findings.recommendation: No change for 015. Make startup required when the fakes are next touched.

findings.title: Production method extracted for a test pin; line pins replaced by a bytecode resolver that matches by callee name
findings.scenario: refusePasswordFieldCount is a verbatim extraction (same condition, POLICY_DENIED, 422, same position at :384), so behaviour is unchanged, but renaming it now breaks a test (intentional). readPrefixSites resolves sites by callee name only (pushContext, translationTransaction, nextAction, program, require) and fails closed unless exactly one lambda$advancePrefix$ qualifies. A new unrelated 'require' between nextAction and the intended one would mis-resolve silently. Evidence says resolved lines 451, 459, 484, 512 equal the live frames.
findings.verified: Read both; read w7 review.md. Did not run.
findings.inferred: That no other require sits between nextAction and its STALE_GENERATION require today.
findings.recommendation: No change. Consider matching owner as well as name if this resolver is extended.

findings.title: Atomic write is correct; the CSI base is still random per JVM; P7 tests only pass inside the full lane
findings.scenario: writeInitialContextState stages next to the target and does ATOMIC_MOVE with REPLACE_EXISTING: correct on POSIX, all ten test-body writers converted, the one plain write at ReplayIT:32628 runs before the runner exists. NEXT_CSI removes the intra-class collision. The base is still 61000 + random(800), so a database that survived across JVMs (not the case for the embedded database today) could still collide at a low rate; no other class uses 61xxx. The two P7 tests fail alone because of the teardown audit scan and @Order (w8 review section 4), a pre-existing coupling.
findings.verified: Read code and grep of Math.random and CSI ranges.
findings.inferred: Embedded database lifetime is one JVM.
findings.recommendation: A fixed base would be deterministic. No action required.

findings.title: Pins now match the image (Node 24.20.0); every host runner step must run on Node 24
findings.scenario: Image record shows node v24.20.0, so the pin move is correct and minimal. The host default is v23.10.0 (/opt/homebrew/bin/node): engine-strict rejects installs and the pins tests fail there (Dex observed this). dist/runtime-versions.json must be regenerated by the gate build. Backend ITs spawn node from PATH and assertObservedBrowserStartup does not check the Node version, so a Node 23 PATH does not break them. Docs that still state Node 22 (GA plan, run log, acceptance register, SPK-04) are listed by Dex for PO. Sample values 'v22.11.0' in RunnerReportProjectionTest and openapi examples are synthetic.
findings.verified: Read fix.patch, the image record, assertObservedBrowserStartup, which node.
findings.inferred: Which Node the live gate's runner steps use.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the gate's runner unit and fixtures steps run under fnm 24.20.0.

findings.title: Three W6 items are outside the bytecode-neutrality receipt, and one test class is non-neutral by design
findings.scenario: The frontend patch (4 files), the ADR-002 section 34 wording change and the @Disabled StudioScheduleApiIT body edit were made before the 'before' snapshot. G2's GuidedWireContractTest gains three private helpers and a reshaped outcomeCases(); 17 call sites read as the same tuples in the same order, and the class passed 18/18 in final-check attempts 01 to 03. Checkstyle config is unchanged against HEAD and no suppression was added. Spotless step neutrality: 1265 classes, 0 differing in code or constants.
findings.verified: Read manifests, source.diff for G1, helper bodies and call sites for G2, XML for attempts 01 to 03, git diff of backend/config.
findings.inferred: Case set of outcomeCases() before the extraction (not stored); relied on Dex's tuple comparison.
